claims.text: When recidivism prevalence differs between two groups, a test-fair risk score cannot achieve equal false positive and false negative rates across those groups simultaneously.
In the Broward County dataset, the 2-year recidivism rate is 51% for Black defendants compared to 39% for White defendants.
In the Broward County dataset, the COMPAS false positive rate is 45% for Black defendants compared to 23% for White defendants.
In the Broward County dataset, the COMPAS false negative rate is 28% for Black defendants compared to 48% for White defendants.
Racial differences in false positive rates for COMPAS persist across prior criminal record count subgroups among defendants charged with misdemeanor offenses.

Under a binary MinMax penalty policy, the expected difference in penalty among non-recidivating individuals across groups equals the sentence differential multiplied by the difference in group false positive rates.
Under a binary MinMax penalty policy, the expected difference in penalty between groups is upper bounded by the total variation distance between the group score distributions.

evidence.description: Mathematical derivation showing FPR = (p / (1 - p)) * ((1 - PPV) / PPV) * (1 - FNR), establishing that equal PPV across groups with unequal prevalence p requires unequal FPR or FNR.
Empirical analysis of Broward County data showing recidivism rates of 51% for Black defendants versus 39% for White defendants.
Tabulated error rates from the ProPublica COMPAS dataset showing Black FPR at 45% and White FPR at 23%.
Tabulated error rates from the ProPublica COMPAS dataset showing Black FNR at 28% and White FNR at 48%.
Figure 2 plots false positive rates across prior count categories (0, 1-3, 4-6, 7-10, >10) for misdemeanor offenses, demonstrating persistent higher FPR for Black defendants.
Formal proof of Corollary 3.1 showing Delta = (tH - tL)(FPR_b - FPR_w) for non-recidivators.
Formal proof of Proposition 3.2 showing Delta <= (tH - tL) d_TV(f_b,y, f_w,y).

methodologies.name: Mathematical Fairness Criterion & Error Rate Decomposition Analysis
methodologies.description: Derivation of exact algebraic relationships between predictive calibration (PPV), group base prevalence, and classification error rates (FPR/FNR), combined with decision-theoretic penalty mapping (MinMax policy).
conditions: Subgroup stratification by prior convictions and offense severity

limitations.text: The formal analytical model focuses on a simplified binary risk score and binary penalty framework.
Balancing error rates at an aggregate level does not guarantee error rate balance within finer sub-populations or prior record categories.
Standard psychometric test-fairness criteria ignore trade-offs with false positive and false negative error rate disparities when base rates differ.

future_work.text: Develop criteria to determine the appropriate subgroup granularity at which error rate balance should be enforced in recidivism risk assessment tools.
